title: File transfer: FTP, SFTP and SCP

videos.script: Sooner or later every job in IT involves moving a file. A new page for the company website. A backup to the office server. A scanner that has to drop its scans somewhere. {{files}} The oldest way is FTP, and it is still everywhere, in hosting accounts and in devices. It is also the one that trips people up. It uses two connections, and it fights with firewalls and NAT. {{ftp}} In its plain form it sends the password where anybody on the way can read it. You will see that happen, and then fix it with FTPS. {{fix}} Then you will move files the way most administrators do today, over SSH. You will use scp for one file and sftp for a session. You will set up an account that can drop files and do nothing else, and use rsync, which sends only what changed. {{ssh}} And you will check, with a checksum, that what arrived is what was sent. {{check}}
